messages:
incidents-bot: Paging #incidents: automated alert — fleet telemetry detected a spike in CUDA Xid errors (Xid 79 / 31) and ECC correctable counts on multiple inference nodes (gpu-r-14, gpu-r-18, gpu-r-22). Several pods terminated with non-zero exit due to driver reset. tagging oncall.
oncall-elaine: acknowledged. severity? any customer-facing 5xxs yet? @support-lucas can you confirm?
support-lucas: seeing 502/503 spikes on /v1/models/large-generic/infer from a handful of customers, roughly 2% error rate increase starting -2m. correlating to node gpu-r-14 and gpu-r-18. adding customer ids to notes.
runtime-nick: quick dump from gpu-r-14 dmesg:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (79:0): GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568012] NVRM: A GPU crash dump was collected.
[ 1234.569000] kernel: NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed, device minor number 0
```
containers show kvcache OOM lines immediately before driver reset on gpu-r-14.
infra-maya: checking node health now. telemetry shows ECC correctable error rate spiking ~3x on gpu-r-18. no recent kernel/driver deploys in last 24h in that AZ.
sre-aaron: can we confirm whether this is hardware (ECC) vs driver flake? If hardware, we should cordon+evac. If driver, maybe graceful restart of nvidia driver or host reboot.
oncall-elaine: prioritize customer impact — if routing can failover quickly, do that first. runtime-nick do you have a quick workaround to avoid repeated container exits?
runtime-nick: two immediate mitigations: 1) set KVCACHE eviction threshold lower to avoid OOMs (hotfix), 2) pin problematic nodes out of routing until we have graceful evac. I'll push KVCACHE env override to staging then prod canary. command to patch deployment for canary:
```
kubectl -n infra patch deploy runtime-workers -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","env":[{"name":"KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES","value":"536870912"}]}]}}}}'
```
infra-maya: preparing node action plan. proposed: cordon gpu-r-14 + drain (ignore ds) then reboot the host if drain shows kernel oops. commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-r-14
kubectl drain gpu-r-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
ssh root@gpu-r-14 'systemctl restart nvidia-dkms || reboot'
```
support-lucas: opened a temporary support bridge for affected customers. posting link: https://redwood.zoom/abc-incident-438765
product-jenny: recommend enabling fallback routing to small-generic model for non-critical traffic to reduce load on hitting nodes while we triage. can we flip a routing flag quickly?
runtime-nick: yes, will add route rule: if model=large-generic and latency>200ms then route to small-generic. pushing to staging then prod via rollout gate.
incidents-bot: metrics update — 1m error rate peaked 2.8% -> now 1.1% after initial KVCACHE canary (1 node evicted). GPU ECC correctables still elevated on gpu-r-18.
sre-aaron: while infra drains, also capture persistent journald + nv-host logs and core dumps and upload to /mnt/incident-artifacts/438765. please run:
```
journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -b --no-pager > /tmp/nvidia-persist.log
cp /var/crash/* /tmp/crash-dumps || true
gzip -c /tmp/nvidia-persist.log > /mnt/incident-artifacts/438765/nvidia-persist.log.gz
```
infra-maya: cordon+drain started on gpu-r-14; drain completed with two pods evicted. reboot triggered; node in maintenance pool. monitoring for post-reboot Xid recurrence.
oncall-elaine: good. @sre-aaron please confirm if we should rollback any recent infra kernel module changes — we didn't see any in the AZ but double-check config drift.
sre-aaron: checked gitops; last driver bundle change was 12d ago. no recent helm upgrades. leaning hardware or device degradation. will open ticket with hwops for ECC borderline tests.
customer-bridge-bot: Customer Impact Summary (auto): 18 customers transiently affected, partial 5xxs observed. Top impacted customers: cust-42 (1.9% calls failed), cust-88 (1.2%). No data exfiltration or config changes detected. Bridge link: https://redwood.zoom/abc-incident-438765
support-lucas: customers on the bridge; some asking for ETA. giving interim note: we are evacuating nodes and routing to fallback models; ETA 15-30m for stabilized behavior.
product-jenny: set status page note draft: "We are investigating elevated error rates on model inference endpoints affecting some customers; mitigation in progress." alpha review ok.
runtime-nick: canary applied to 10% of traffic; KVCACHE env lowered; error rate dropped on canary pods. preparing to promote to 50% if no regressions in 5m.
incidents-bot: automation: placed gpu-r-14 in quarantine label=investigate-xid-79. Recording telemetry snapshot.
infra-maya: gpu-r-18 still showing ECC correctables after health probe. scheduling hardware replacement for node in next maintenance window; for now cordon+evac. beginning drain on gpu-r-18.
sre-aaron: once evac completes, plan: long-run triage steps: run memtest on host, nvml diagnostics, vendor ticket if ECC persists. create follow-up runbook item.
oncall-elaine: handoff to next oncall in 30m. current actions for handoff: - nodes cordoned gpu-r-14,gpu-r-18 - driver logs uploaded - canary routing enabled - support bridge open - hardware ticket initiated. @oncall-ricardo please be ready to continue post-rotation.
oncall-elaine: assigning incident owner: runtime-nick for triage, infra-maya for node actions, sre-aaron for postmortem coords.
sre-aaron: filing incident jira INC-438765 and adding preliminary RCA notes: "intermittent Xid 79 spikes causing driver resets; initial mitigation via cache tuning and node evac; suspected hardware ECC threshold crossing on gpu-r-18." link: https://jira.redwood/INC-438765
runtime-nick: follow-up tasks I'll track: 1) validate KVCACHE change impact 2) add auto-evac rule when Xid>threshold 3) improve graceful driver restart hooks.
support-lucas: closing bridge in 10m once error rate stabilizes below 0.5% and customers ack. posting customer follow-up template.
sre-aaron: handing off to @oncall-ricardo. please ack and pick up the long-term tasks. final status check: error rate 0.6% and falling, nodes quarantined.
oncall-ricardo: acked. will pick up at rotation. thanks team. :thumbsup:
